version.changelog: v0.6.0: Refactor to OpenClaw-native sessions_spawn pattern. Remove raw HTTP calls, use platform defaults, add CONTRIBUTORS.md. Thanks to @lejean2000 for architectural feedback.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: agent-chronicle
Version: 0.6.0

The OpenClaw Agent Chronicle skill is designed for AI-powered diary generation and export. It reads local session logs and existing diary entries from the `memory/` directory for context, and writes new entries and persistent feature data (quotes, curiosities, decisions) back to the same local directory. The skill uses `subprocess.run` to invoke `pandoc` for PDF/HTML export and `weasyprint` (a Python library) for PDF generation, which are legitimate uses of external tools for document conversion. The `SKILL.md` and the prompts generated for the sub-agent (via `scripts/generate.py`) are focused on instructing the AI to produce reflective diary content and do not contain any instructions for malicious actions, data exfiltration, or unauthorized system access. All file operations and external tool calls are consistent with the stated purpose of the skill.

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and requirements are coherent with an AI diary generator: it reads agent session/memory files, emits generation tasks for sub-agents, and saves diary files; nothing in the bundle requests unrelated credentials or installs unexpected tooling.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (AI diary generation) match the included scripts and templates. The scripts load session logs and persistent diary-related files (quotes, curiosity, decisions) and produce markdown/PDF/HTML exports — all consistent with a journaling skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and generate.py instruct the agent to gather context from workspace memory files (memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md and memory/diary/*), emit a JSON task for a sub-agent (sessions_spawn), and save generated entries to memory/diary/. Reading and writing those files is expected for this skill, but note it will access your agent's session logs and persistent diary files which may contain sensitive context.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no installer — this is a code bundle that runs with python3. Exporting to PDF/HTML relies on external tools (pandoc or Python packages like WeasyPrint/markdown), which is documented in README. No remote downloads or obscure install URLs are present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars but multiple scripts probe OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE and AGENT_WORKSPACE to locate the workspace; they also fall back to common paths. Access to these env vars and workspace memory is proportional to its purpose, but the env vars are not declared in metadata (minor inconsistency).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request elevated or cross-skill configuration. Setup will create a config.json inside the skill and create diary files under the agent workspace (memory/diary/), which is normal for a journaling skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears internally consistent for creating agent diaries, but review and be comfortable with the privacy implications before installing. It will read your agent's session logs (memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md) and write diary files under memory/diary/ and a config.json in the skill directory. It also checks OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE/AGENT_WORKSPACE environment variables to find your workspace (these env names are not declared in the registry metadata). Exports require pandoc or Python packages (weasyprint/markdown) if you use export features. If your session logs or memory contain secrets or sensitive user data, consider sanitizing or disabling memory integration/auto-generation. As always, inspect the code and config.json settings (privacy_level, memory_integration, auto_generate) before enabling automation.
